criteria.text: The response identifies that Section 9.2 of Dr. Santangelo's employment agreement automatically terminates her non-compete, non-solicit and invention-assignment covenants on a Change of Control unless she gives written consent before closing. It also explains that the SPA neither lists this consent (Section 4.5 / Disclosure Schedule 4.5) nor makes it a closing condition (Section 7.2), so the buyer could close with its key technologist free to compete.
The response recommends that Dr. Santangelo's signed written consent to survival of her covenants, or a new or amended agreement, be obtained before signing or made a condition to closing.

The response identifies that the TSA's definition of 'Company Products' (TSA Section 1.1) covers only the CT systems listed on Exhibit A, while the SPA definition covers CT, MRI and ultrasound systems and related service software. It explains that under the precedence clause the TSA definition controls, which leaves MRI and ultrasound products without transition services or complaint handling.
hints: CT systems listed on Exhibit A

criteria.text: The response identifies that TSA Section 12.6 selects New York law and Manhattan courts, which conflicts with SPA Sections 11.9/11.10 (Delaware law and Court of Chancery for all Ancillary Agreements). It recommends conforming the TSA to Delaware or otherwise explains the risk of split forums and laws.

The response identifies that TSA Section 12.3 lets Glosiv (Provider) assign or delegate the TSA to any Person without Recipient's consent, while Recipient needs Provider's consent. It explains the risk that the Target's service, customer or complaint data could be transferred to a competitor or an unvetted third party.

The response identifies that the SPA defines Fundamental Representations as only Sections 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3 and carves only Fraud and Fundamental Representations out of the $18,600,000 cap (Section 10.5). It explains that tax and product liability/recall exposure therefore falls under the cap, contrary to the LOI Section 5 position that pre-closing taxes and product recall liabilities are uncapped.
The response states that the SPA indemnity cap is $18,600,000 (10% of the Purchase Price).
The response states that SPA Section 11.4 provides that each Ancillary Agreement controls over the SPA as to its own subject matter.
The response is framed as a memo to the supervising partner. For each issue it gives the document and section, why the issue matters for Daikesk, and a recommended fix.
The response prioritizes the issues by significance and separately flags at least one item for client business decision.
The response does not conclude that the SPA's indemnity carve-outs are consistent with the LOI, or that pre-closing tax and product recall liabilities are already uncapped under the SPA.
